import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define source file paths

        "Source9_12_6": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_12/test_6.csv",

        "Source9_12_9": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_12/test_9.csv",
        "Source9_12_10": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_12/test_10.csv",
    }

    # Load all source tables into dataframes
    # We will read only the relevant columns and rename them to avoid conflicts
    # Each source has columns: ['2012-12-05', <value_column>]
    # We will keep '2012-12-05' as the join key and rename the value column to its name

    dfs = {}
    for key, path in source_files.items():
        df = pd.read_csv(path)
        # Drop any unnamed index columns if present
        df = df.loc[:, ~df.columns.str.contains('^Unnamed')]
        # Identify the value column (other than '2012-12-05')
        value_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col != '2012-12-05']
        if len(value_cols) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected number of value columns in {key}: {value_cols}")
        value_col = value_cols[0]
        # Rename value column to its name (to keep consistent)
        df = df.rename(columns={value_col: value_col})
        dfs[key] = df

    # Start merging all dataframes on '2012-12-05'
    # Source9_12_0 has columns ['2012-12-05', '301.0'] (integer column)
    # Others have ['2012-12-05', <float column>]
    # We will do left merges sequentially starting from Source9_12_0

    # Initialize merged_df with Source9_12_0
    merged_df = dfs["Source9_12_0"]

    # List of sources to merge (excluding Source9_12_0)
    merge_order = [
        "Source9_12_1",
        "Source9_12_2",
        "Source9_12_3",
        "Source9_12_4",
        "Source9_12_5",
        "Source9_12_6",
        "Source9_12_7",
        "Source9_12_8",
        "Source9_12_9",
        "Source9_12_10",
    ]

    for key in merge_order:
        df_to_merge = dfs[key]
        # Merge on '2012-12-05' with left join to keep all rows from merged_df
        merged_df = pd.merge(
            merged_df,
            df_to_merge,
            on="2012-12-05",
            how="left",
            validate="one_to_one",
            suffixes=("", f"_{key}")
        )
        # After merge, no duplicate columns expected because each source has unique value column

    # Rename columns to match target schema exactly
    # Target schema columns:
    # ['2012-12-05': string, '301.0': integer, '0.0075805085': float, '0.0179': float, '6.9': float,
    #  '0.17657143': float, '20.3333': float, '0.016157143': float, '242.364': float, '0.1646': float,
    #  '0.7268': float, '0.4332': float]

    # The columns in merged_df should be:
    # '2012-12-05', '301.0', '0.016157143', '242.364', '0.1646', '0.4332', '20.3333',
    # '0.0075805085', '6.9', '0.0179', '0.17657143', '0.7268'

    # But order might differ, so reorder columns accordingly

    target_columns_order = [
        '2012-12-05',
        '301.0',
        '0.0075805085',
        '0.0179',
        '6.9',
        '0.17657143',
        '20.3333',
        '0.016157143',
        '242.364',
        '0.1646',
        '0.7268',
        '0.4332',
    ]

    # Check if all target columns exist in merged_df
    missing_cols = [col for col in target_columns_order if col not in merged_df.columns]
    if missing_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing columns after merge: {missing_cols}")

    # Reorder columns
    merged_df = merged_df[target_columns_order]

    # Convert data types according to target schema
    # '2012-12-05': string (date string)
    merged_df['2012-12-05'] = merged_df['2012-12-05'].astype(str)

    # '301.0': integer
    # Some values might be float or missing, convert carefully
    merged_df['301.0'] = pd.to_numeric(merged_df['301.0'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)
